paper.title: Online Learning in a Contract Selection Problem

settings.name_in_paper: Online contract selection with variable number of offers (cost c(m) of offering m contracts)
unmapped: Seller offers an ordered bundle of contracts in (0,1]; buyer with i.i.d. type theta ~ density f (bounded by f_max) accepts the contract maximizing its known payoff U_b(x,theta)
Ordered-preferences assumption: acceptance regions are intervals with boundaries g(x_{i-1},x_i), g Hölder with constant L and exponent alpha
Seller knows the buyer payoff function U_b (hence g)
Learner may offer more than m contracts at a time (in exploration) at increasing cost c(n); regret includes offering cost
Algorithm tuning uses f_max, L, alpha
settings.definition_quote: In an online contract selection problem there is a seller who offers a bundle of $m \in \{1,2,\ldots\}$ contracts ... The buyer who arrives at time $t$ has type $\theta_t$ ... drawn according to the probability density function $f(\theta)$ on $[0,1]$ independently ... R^{alg}(T) = T (U(x^*) - c(m)) - E^{alg}[ \sum_{t=1}^T r(x(t)) - c(m(t))]

settings.name_in_paper: Online contract selection with fixed number of offers m
unmapped: Seller offers exactly m ordered contracts in (0,1] each round; buyer with i.i.d. type theta ~ density f (bounded by f_max) accepts the contract maximizing its known payoff U_b(x,theta)
Ordered-preferences assumption: acceptance-region boundaries g Hölder with constant L and exponent alpha
Seller knows the buyer payoff function U_b (hence g)
Algorithm tuning uses f_max, L, alpha
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we are interested in the case when the seller is limited to offering $m$ contracts at every time step.

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: The regret of the seller using TLVO with time horizon $T$ is upper bounded by R(T) \leq 5 m f_{\max} L 2^{\alpha/2} n_T^{-\alpha} (T-N(T)) + N(T) (U(x^*) + c(n_T) - c(m)) + 2 n_T \sum_{t=1}^T e^{\frac{- f^2_{\max} L^2 2^{\alpha} N(t)}{n_T^{2+ 2\alpha}}}.

results.notes: Bound depends on algorithm-internal quantities N(T), N(t) and n_T. Regret defined via expected payoffs U, so pseudo-regret.
